summary: Oldřich Hujer (1880–1942) was a Czech linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Josef Zubatý and also studied at Leipzig under August Leskien. He taught at Charles University from 1911, serving as ordinary professor from 1924 to 1942.

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner around 2005–2009 and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (Ph.D.). He held posts at Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard as professor (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study as professor (1990–1998).
Olha Dobrodum is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Odesa University in 2015 and has held a post at the State University of Trade and Economics.

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at London Hospital (M.D.), he served as deputy surgeon-general in the Army Medical Department (1859–1885) and later as librarian for the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (1891–1919).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ceylon and earned his Ph.D. at SOAS under William Stede. In 1943, he became Head of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon.

Oliver Hellwig specializes in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. He completed his habilitation under Harry Falk and has held posts at the University of Düsseldorf and the University of Zurich (attested 2024–2025).
Oliver Petersen (born 1961) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang around 1983–2003 and held a post at the Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg around 1983.

Oliver Philipp Frey is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied and served as predoc assistant (2013–2016) at the University of Vienna, and became an SNSF Postdoc.Mobility Fellow at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2023–2025).
Olivia Porter works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at King's College London until 2023 and was appointed Teaching Fellow at the University of Leeds in 2025.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) specialized in Indology and philosophy. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, he held posts at Ankara University (1939–1944), University of Lille (1947–1959), EPHE (1955–1971), and as professor of comparative philosophy at the University of Paris (1960–1974).

Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He has been affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 1992 and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (2004–2005).

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Tord Olsson, Karl H. Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner at Washington, Harvard, and Copenhagen, and served at Lund University.
Olli Littunen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned a BA at Leiden University (2016–2022) and has pursued doctoral research there under Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Olof August Danielsson (1852–1933) was a Swedish linguist and Indologist. He earned his M.A. and Ph.D. at Uppsala University and studied under Ernst Windisch and Bruno Lindner. Danielsson was appointed professor of Greek language and literature at Uppsala in 1891.

Om Prakash is an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. He held teaching posts at Kirori Mal College, the University of Delhi, and the Delhi School of Economics as professor of economic history.

On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a Japanese sinologist. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1902) and the University of Leipzig (~1907–1909), and later held a post at Tokyo Imperial University (~1920–1939).
Ondřej Novák (1946–1977) was a Czech scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. there between approximately 1964 and 1975.

Onorio Ferrero de Gubernatis Ventimiglia (1908–1989) was an Indologist. He taught Oriental languages and cultures at the National University of San Marcos and at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru from 1952 to 1976.

Oreste Nazari (1866–1923) was an Italian Indologist and linguist who studied under Gaspare Gorresio. He taught at the University of Turin (~1898–1923) and served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative history of languages at the University of Palermo (1901–1923).
